introduction.definition: An alumina storage silo stores smelter-grade alumina. An aerated floor of air-slide pads fluidises the product so it flows to the discharge; a bin-vent filter releases displaced air during filling, and trucks or rail cars are loaded below.
applications: Product storage at refineries, ports and smelters

video_tutorials.title: Alumina Storage Silo — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Alumina Storage Silo.
An alumina storage silo stores smelter-grade alumina.
An aerated floor of air-slide pads fluidises the product so it flows to the discharge; a bin-vent filter releases displaced air during filling, and trucks or rail cars are loaded below.
Typical applications include product storage at refineries, ports and smelters; buffer storage before ship or rail loading.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Silo Shell, Roof & Concrete Skirt (with truck drive-through).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Alumina Storage Silo — Operation

script.narration: How the Alumina Storage Silo works.
Alumina fills from the top.
It is stored in the silo.
Air-slide pads fluidise it.
It discharges to the tanker.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Low-pressure air (typically a few hundred mbar) blown through porous air-slide pads fluidises the alumina above the floor so it flows to the discharge without bridging or rat-holing.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Alumina Storage Silo.
Check level and filter ΔP.
Check aeration pads.
Structural inspection.
Watch for bridging/rat-holing: no flow. Common cause: failed aeration.
Watch for overfill: dust release. Common cause: level failure.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
